senses.gloss: renovation, the first stage of the crescent moon.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2:11">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵈ</cite> <he>הרואה … בחִידּוּשָׁהּ</he> he who sees the moon in her first stage.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 1:2:4">Y. Shek. I, 46ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>שמרהו שיבוא בחִידּוּשׁוֹ</he> observe it that it (the maturing of the crops) should coincide with the first part of the month of Nisan.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 25a:10">R. Hash. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>אין חִדּוּשָׁהּ של לבנה וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <cite ref="H00220"><he>חָדְשָׁהּ</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="H00219"><he>חֹדֶשׁ</he></cite>) the renovation of the moon takes no less than twenty nine days and a half &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:2:14">Y. Taan. II, 65ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>ח׳ בית וכ׳</he> the restoration of thy sanctuary.
<cite ref="Chagigah 3a:15">Ḥag. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>א״א לבה״מ בלא ח׳</he> it is impossible for a college session to pass without a novel remark.
<cite ref="Chagigah 3a:15">Ib.</cite> <he>מה ח׳ היה וכ׳</he> what was the news in college to-day?—

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:16:1">Cant. R. to IV, 16</cite> <he>ובואי דבר של ח׳</he> ‘and come’ (<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:16:1">ib.</cite>) intimates a novel rule (adding thanks-offerings); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:11:5">Y. Meg. I, 72ᶜ</cite> top, a. e.—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 13">Lev. R. s. 13</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00218"><he>חָדָשׁ</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: strange law, exception, unique law (which allows of no conclusion by analogy), anomaly.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 27a:3">Snh. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>עד זומם ח׳ הוא וכ׳</he> the law concerning the punishment of false witnesses is an anomaly, (for why must we trust the one set more than the other?) <he>אין … חִידּוּשׁוֹ ואילך</he> therefore you cannot go beyond what it says distinctly, i.e. previous evidences of refuted witnesses cannot be assailed.

<cite ref="Pesachim 44b:8-9">Pes. 44ᵇ</cite> <he>מבשר וחלב … דח׳ הוא</he> you can draw no analogy from the law concerning the mixture of flesh and milk, for it is an anomaly; <he>ומאי חידושו</he> and wherein is it an anomaly? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 7:1:3">Y. Ter. VII, beg. 44ᶜ</cite> <he>לחִידּוּשׁוֹ יצא</he> the law (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:13">Deut. XXII, 13</cite> sq.) is specified for its anomalous nature; a. fr.
